newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe police arrest doctor over strike.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe police arrest doctor over strike.

text.p: Zimbabwean police said on Tuesday they have arrested a junior doctor on charges of inciting a nationwide strike by state-employed nurses which has paralysed public health facilities.
"Farai Jiah was picked up last night (Monday) on allegations of inciting nurses to strike," Assistant Inspector Michael Munyikwa told Reuters.

He said Jiah, chairman of the state Hospital Doctors Association, would appear in court "soon". The official news agency ZIANA reported that junior doctors had gone on strike to protest a tJiah's arrest. None of them could be located for comment.

The doctors -- who went on strike with the nurses on August 21 to press for higher pay, allowances and negotiations on their working conditions -- went back to work last week after the government threatened to sack them.
The government subsequently sacked the nurses -- estimated by union officials at 10,000 -- for ignoring its order.

Zimbabwe state media says the number of patients dying from lack of attention is mounting daily in public hospitals, where senior doctors have been handling emergencies only with help from army medical personnel and the Red Cross.
